case.case_title: Priyantha and others v Ceylon Petroleum Corporation and others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. No. 103/2002 FR, decided on 2 July 2003

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the termination of the petitioners' services pursuant to a Cabinet decision invalidating appointments and promotions during a specific period violated their fundamental rights under Article 12(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners argued that the Cabinet decision of 26.12.2001 did not apply to them because they were reinstated in service rather than newly appointed or promoted, and thus their termination violated their right to equality and equal protection under Article 12(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the Cabinet decision invalidating all appointments and promotions during the period between the dissolution of Parliament and the General Election applied to the petitioners, justifying termination of their services.
key_facts: Petitioners were Security Assistants recruited mainly on contract after 1988.
They participated in industrial action in August 2000 demanding permanency and were summarily terminated on 22.8.2000.
They were reinstated on 17.12.2001 on the same terms and conditions during the period between dissolution and General Election.
They were made permanent effective 01.10.2001 based on a Public Administration Circular.
The Cabinet decision of 26.12.2001 invalidated all appointments and promotions during the relevant period but was suspended and reviewed on 30.01.2002.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that the Cabinet decision was directed at preventing surplus recruitment and improper promotions, and did not apply to bona fide reinstatements following dismissal. Article 12(1) protects against arbitrary and unreasonable termination violating equality before the law and equal protection.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioners' reinstatement was not an appointment or promotion but a remedy for an arguably disproportionate penalty. The termination based on the Cabinet decision was arbitrary and unreasonable, especially after the decision was suspended and reviewed, thus violating Article 12(1).
principles_established: Cabinet decisions invalidating appointments and promotions must be applied only to those categories and not to bona fide reinstatements.
Termination of service must not be arbitrary or unreasonable to comply with Article 12(1).
Reinstatement following industrial action dismissal can be justified and protected under fundamental rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the termination of the petitioners' services violated Article 12(1) and ordered their reinstatement without back wages but with benefits of voluntary retirement schemes offered to comparable employees.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Reinstatement of petitioners with effect from 1 October 2003 without break in service, no back wages, and offer of voluntary retirement scheme benefits; payment of costs of Rs. 25,000/- to petitioners.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as it protects individuals from arbitrary termination and ensures equal protection under the law. The court found the termination violated this constitutional guarantee.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The termination of the services of the petitioners by letters dated 13.01.2002, and the failure to rescind such termination after the second Cabinet decision was arbitrary and unreasonable, and in violation of Article 12(1).
